  • Cost of goods sold:
    • This is calculated in the Trading Account, not the Manufacturing Account. The cost of goods sold includes the cost of finished goods sold during the period.
    • It is derived by adding the cost of purchases to the opening stock and then subtracting the closing stock.
  • Gross profit:
    • Gross profit is calculated in the Trading Account by subtracting the cost of goods sold from the sales revenue.
    • It indicates the profitability of core business activities before deducting operating expenses.
  • Net profit:
    • Net profit is determined in the Profit and Loss Account after accounting for all operating expenses, non-operating incomes, and non-operating expenses.
    • It represents the overall profitability of the business.

questions.question: Which of the following is regarded as an accounting convention and NOT as an accounting concept?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is regarded as an accounting convention and NOT as an accounting concept?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Conservatism.

Key Points

  • Conservatism:
    • The conservatism principle, also known as prudence, is an accounting convention that advises accountants to exercise caution and choose solutions that result in lower profits and asset valuations. This principle aims to prevent the overstatement of financial health.
    • It ensures that uncertainties and risks are adequately reflected in financial statements, promoting reliability and accuracy.
    • For example, if there are two equally probable outcomes for a future event, the one that is less likely to overstate assets and income should be chosen.

Additional Information

  • Going concern:
    • This accounting concept assumes that a business will continue to operate indefinitely, or at least for the foreseeable future. It implies that the company has no intention or need to liquidate or significantly curtail its operations.
  • Money measurement:
    • This concept states that only those transactions and events that can be measured in monetary terms are recorded in the financial statements. Non-monetary items like employee skills or customer satisfaction are not recorded.
  • Accounting period:
    • This concept divides the life of an enterprise into time periods, such as months, quarters, or years, for the purpose of preparing financial statements. It ensures that financial performance and position are reported periodically.

questions.question: The salary paid to Mr. Virat, a clerk, for the month of August 2023, debited to the furniture account instead of the salary account will be regarded as a / an _______.
questions.questionHtml: The salary paid to Mr. Virat, a clerk, for the month of August 2023, debited to the furniture account instead of the salary account will be regarded as a / an _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is error of principle.

Key Points

  • Error of Principle:
    • This type of error occurs when a transaction is recorded in violation of accounting principles. In this case, the salary expense, which should be recorded in the salary account, is incorrectly debited to the furniture account.
    • Errors of principle usually involve the incorrect classification of accounts, leading to inaccurate financial statements.
    • These errors are often more serious than other types because they can significantly distort the financial position of the enterprise.

Additional Information

  • Error of Omission:
    • This error occurs when a transaction is completely omitted from the accounting records. In this scenario, the transaction is recorded but in the wrong account.
  • Compensating Error:
    • These are errors that counterbalance each other. For example, an overstatement of one account may be offset by an understatement of another. This is not applicable here as only one transaction is incorrectly recorded.
  • Error of Commission:
    • This type of error occurs when an entry is made in the correct type of account but in the wrong account. For example, debiting the wrong customer account in accounts receivable. The given scenario involves an error in the type of account, not just the wrong account within the same category.

questions.question: Which of the following methods does NOT consider historical cost of inventory?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following methods does NOT consider historical cost of inventory?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Retail price method.

Key Points

  • Retail Price Method:
    • The retail price method estimates the ending inventory value based on the current retail prices, rather than the historical cost.
    • This method uses the relationship between the cost and the retail price to value inventory, which can be particularly useful in retail businesses with large inventories.
    • Since it does not rely on historical costs, it is not affected by changes in purchase prices over time, making it the correct answer.

Additional Information

  • FIFO (First-In, First-Out):
    • This method assumes that the oldest inventory items are sold first, and thus, the cost of goods sold is based on the historical cost of the oldest inventory.
    • It ensures that the inventory on hand is valued at the most recent costs.
  • LIFO (Last-In, First-Out):
    • Under LIFO, the most recently purchased or produced items are considered sold first, making the cost of goods sold based on the historical cost of the latest inventory.
    • This method can result in lower net income during inflationary periods as it matches current costs with current revenues.
  • Weighted Average:
    • The weighted average method calculates the cost of goods sold and ending inventory based on the average cost of all units available for sale during the period.
    • This average cost takes into account the historical cost of all inventory items.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

options.text: The amount of depreciation charged on a machinery item is debited to the depreciation account.
options.html: The amount of depreciation charged on a machinery item is debited to the depreciation account.

options.text: Depreciation means decrease in the value of an asset.
options.html: Depreciation means decrease in the value of an asset.

options.text: In the reducing balance method, the amount charged to depreciation declines.
options.html: In the reducing balance method, the amount charged to depreciation declines.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Depreciation is a cash item.

Key Points

  • Depreciation is a cash item:
    • This statement is incorrect. Depreciation is a non-cash expense. It represents the allocation of the cost of a tangible asset over its useful life and does not involve any actual cash outflow.
    • Depreciation is recorded in the financial statements to match the cost of the asset with the revenue it generates, adhering to the matching principle in accounting.
    • Being a non-cash item, depreciation impacts the net income but not the cash flow directly.

Additional Information

  • The amount of depreciation charged on a machinery item is debited to the depreciation account:
    • This statement is correct. The depreciation expense is debited to the depreciation account, which is an expense account, and credited to the accumulated depreciation account, which is a contra-asset account.
  • Depreciation means decrease in the value of an asset:
    • This statement is correct. Depreciation reflects the reduction in the value of an asset over time due to wear and tear, obsolescence, or other factors.
  • In the reducing balance method, the amount charged to depreciation declines:
    • This statement is correct. In the reducing balance method (also known as the declining balance method), depreciation is calculated as a fixed percentage of the book value of the asset, which decreases each year. As a result, the depreciation expense declines over time.

questions.question: In relation to the single-entry system, which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
questions.questionHtml: In relation to the single-entry system, which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

options.text: The single - entry system is considered as an incomplete bookkeeping system, as it does not record two aspects of financial transactions of a business.
options.html: The single - entry system is considered as an incomplete bookkeeping system, as it does not record two aspects of financial transactions of a business.

options.text: Since the single - entry system is not based on the principles of credit and debit, it fails to give the arithmetical accuracy of books of accounts.
options.html: Since the single - entry system is not based on the principles of credit and debit, it fails to give the arithmetical accuracy of books of accounts.

options.text: The single - entry system is a scientific and systematic system of recording and maintaining financial transactions.
options.html: The single - entry system is a scientific and systematic system of recording and maintaining financial transactions.

options.text: The single - entry system of bookkeeping is easy to maintain and simple to understand.
options.html: The single - entry system of bookkeeping is easy to maintain and simple to understand.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is The single - entry system is a scientific and systematic system of recording and maintaining financial transactions.

Key Points

  • The single-entry system is a scientific and systematic system of recording and maintaining financial transactions:
    • This statement is incorrect. The single-entry system is not considered scientific or systematic because it does not follow the double-entry principles of accounting, which require recording both the debit and credit aspects of every transaction.
    • It is often referred to as an incomplete or unsystematic method of bookkeeping.
    • Due to its lack of a structured framework, it is prone to errors and may not provide a comprehensive view of a business’s financial health.

Additional Information

  • The single-entry system is considered as an incomplete bookkeeping system, as it does not record two aspects of financial transactions of a business:
    • This is a correct statement. The single-entry system records only one side of each transaction, typically focusing on cash inflows and outflows.
    • It does not capture the double-entry aspect, which includes both debits and credits, making it incomplete.
  • Since the single-entry system is not based on the principles of credit and debit, it fails to give the arithmetical accuracy of books of accounts:
    • This statement is correct. The lack of a double-entry mechanism means it does not provide a trial balance, making it difficult to ensure the arithmetical accuracy of the accounts.
    • This can lead to discrepancies and undetected errors in the financial records.
  • The single-entry system of bookkeeping is easy to maintain and simple to understand:
    • This statement is correct. One of the main advantages of the single-entry system is its simplicity.
    • It is often used by small businesses and individuals who do not have extensive accounting knowledge.
    • The system requires less effort and fewer resources to maintain compared to the double-entry system.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT regarded as a revenue expenditure?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is NOT regarded as a revenue expenditure?

options.text: Expenses incurred as lawyer's fee to defend a suit claiming that the firm's factory site belonged to the Plaintiff. The suit was not successful.
options.html: Expenses incurred as lawyer's fee to defend a suit claiming that the firm's factory site belonged to the Plaintiff. The suit was not successful.

options.text: Expenses incurred in connection with obtaining a licensee for starting a factory.
options.html: Expenses incurred in connection with obtaining a licensee for starting a factory.

options.text: Expenses incurred for removal of stock to a new site.
options.html: Expenses incurred for removal of stock to a new site.

options.text: Expenses incurred to change rings and pistons of an engine to get full efficiency.
options.html: Expenses incurred to change rings and pistons of an engine to get full efficiency.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Expenses incurred in connection with obtaining a license for starting a factory.

Key Points

  • Expenses incurred in connection with obtaining a license for starting a factory:
    • This is considered a capital expenditure because it is a one-time cost associated with setting up the business and acquiring a long-term asset. It provides benefits over a long period and is not a recurring expense.

Additional Information

  • Expenses incurred as lawyer's fee to defend a suit claiming that the firm's factory site belonged to the Plaintiff. The suit was not successful:
    • This is a revenue expenditure as it is a recurring cost associated with the normal operations of the business. It does not result in the acquisition of a long-term asset.
  • Expenses incurred for removal of stock to a new site:
    • This is also a revenue expenditure. It is a cost associated with the day-to-day operations of the business and does not provide long-term benefits.
  • Expenses incurred to change rings and pistons of an engine to get full efficiency:
    • This is considered a revenue expenditure as it is a maintenance cost aimed at ensuring the asset (engine) continues to operate efficiently. It does not extend the life of the asset but maintains its current operational capacity.

questions.question: The meaning of _______ is freedom for economic decisions, which means that all the producers, owners and consumers of factors of production are free to take their decisions to promote their self - interest.
questions.questionHtml: The meaning of _______ is freedom for economic decisions, which means that all the producers, owners and consumers of factors of production are free to take their decisions to promote their self - interest.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is economic liberalisation.

Key Points

  • Economic Liberalisation:
    • Economic liberalisation refers to the process of reducing government interventions and restrictions in an economy.
    • This allows for greater participation of private enterprises in economic activities, fostering competition, efficiency, and innovation.
    • It includes the deregulation of industries, reduction of trade barriers, and the privatisation of state-owned enterprises, thereby providing producers, owners, and consumers the freedom to make economic decisions independently.

Additional Information

  • Privatisation:
    • Privatisation refers to the transfer of ownership of property or businesses from a government to a privately-owned entity.While it can be a part of economic liberalisation, it does not encompass the entire concept of freedom for economic decisions.
  • Globalisation:
    • Globalisation is the process of interaction and integration among people, companies, and governments worldwide.It focuses more on international trade and cultural exchange rather than the internal freedom of economic decision-making.
  • Corporatisation:
    • Corporatisation involves transforming state-owned enterprises into corporations or companies.
    • It is a specific form of reform and does not necessarily imply the broader scope of economic freedom addressed by economic liberalisation.

questions.question: If the proportionate change in supply is more than proportionate change in the price, it is said to be:
questions.questionHtml: If the proportionate change in supply is more than proportionate change in the price, it is said to be:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is relatively elastic supply.

Key Points

  • Relatively elastic supply:
    • When the proportionate change in supply is more than the proportionate change in price, it indicates that suppliers are very responsive to price changes.
    • This situation is termed as relatively elastic supply, meaning that a small change in price leads to a larger change in the quantity supplied.
    • In financial enterprises, this could be observed in markets where production can be increased or decreased quickly without significant cost, such as the market for digital products or services.

Additional Information

  • Perfectly elastic supply:
    • This is incorrect. Perfectly elastic supply means that suppliers are willing to supply any amount of goods at a specific price, and any change in price will cause the supply to drop to zero or become infinite. This is an extreme and rare situation.
  • Relatively inelastic supply:
    • This is incorrect. Relatively inelastic supply means that the proportionate change in supply is less than the proportionate change in price. Suppliers are not very responsive to price changes in this case.
  • Unitary elastic supply:
    • This is incorrect. Unitary elastic supply means that the proportionate change in supply is exactly equal to the proportionate change in price. The supply responsiveness is directly proportional to price changes.

questions.question: In relation to the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003, '_______' means the gross domestic product reckoned at constant prices, as published by the Central Statistics Office from time to time.
questions.questionHtml: In relation to the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003, '_______' means the gross domestic product reckoned at constant prices, as published by the Central Statistics Office from time to time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Real gross domestic product

Key Points

  • Real gross domestic product:
    • Real gross domestic product (GDP) is the measure of a country's economic output adjusted for price changes (inflation or deflation). It reflects the value of all goods and services produced by an economy at constant prices, providing a more accurate representation of economic performance over time.
    • In the context of the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003, using real GDP allows for a consistent comparison of economic data by removing the effects of price level changes.
    • Real GDP is published by the Central Statistics Office (CSO) and serves as a crucial metric for policymakers to design and implement fiscal policies aimed at sustainable economic growth.

Additional Information

  • Notional gross domestic product:
    • This term is not commonly used in economic analysis. The correct term is nominal GDP, which measures a country's economic output using current prices, without adjusting for inflation. Nominal GDP can be misleading for long-term comparisons due to price level changes.
  • Secondary gross domestic product:
    • This is not a recognized economic term. GDP is generally categorized into primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors, but there is no specific measure called secondary GDP.
  • Residual gross domestic product:
    • This term does not exist in standard economic terminology. Residuals in economic models usually refer to the unexplained portion of a regression model, not a type of GDP measurement.

questions.question: Which of the following is regarded as a supervisory function of the Reserve Bank of India?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is regarded as a supervisory function of the Reserve Bank of India?

options.text: Implementation of the deposit insurance scheme
options.html: Implementation of the deposit insurance scheme

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Implementation of the deposit insurance scheme.

Key Points

  • Implementation of the deposit insurance scheme:
    • The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) oversees the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC), which provides deposit insurance. This is a supervisory function to ensure the stability and safety of the banking system.
    • The DICGC insures all bank deposits, such as savings, fixed, current, and recurring deposits, ensuring that depositors are protected in case of bank failures.
    • This function is critical for maintaining public confidence in the banking system.

Additional Information

  • Banker to the government:
    • This is a key function of the RBI but not a supervisory function. The RBI manages the banking needs of the central and state governments, including managing their accounts and public debt.
  • Exchange rate management:
    • The RBI is responsible for managing the exchange rate of the Indian Rupee. It involves interventions in the foreign exchange market to stabilize the currency. However, this is not a supervisory function.
  • Issue of currency notes:
    • The RBI has the sole authority to issue currency notes in India. This function ensures the supply of adequate and quality currency notes but does not fall under the supervisory functions of the RBI.

questions.question: In relation to Production Possibilities Curve (PPC), which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
questions.questionHtml: In relation to Production Possibilities Curve (PPC), which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

options.text: If the PPC curve is not a straight line, the opportunity cost is constant.
options.html: If the PPC curve is not a straight line, the opportunity cost is constant.

options.text: The PPC is also called production possibility boundary.
options.html: The PPC is also called production possibility boundary.

options.text: Shift of the PPC curve is nothing but economic growth.
options.html: Shift of the PPC curve is nothing but economic growth.

options.text: Any point that lies below the PPC curve is a possible combination. But if the economy is working below the PPC curve that indicates the unused resources or unemployment.
options.html: Any point that lies below the PPC curve is a possible combination. But if the economy is working below the PPC curve that indicates the unused resources or unemployment.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is If the PPC curve is not a straight line, the opportunity cost is constant.

Key Points

  • If the PPC curve is not a straight line, the opportunity cost is constant:
    • This statement is incorrect. If the PPC curve is not a straight line, it implies that the opportunity cost is not constant. Instead, it varies depending on the combination of goods being produced. A bowed-outward (concave) PPC indicates increasing opportunity costs, meaning more of one good must be given up to produce additional units of the other good.
    • In a financial enterprise context, this concept is crucial for making decisions about resource allocation. For example, if a company allocates resources to different projects, the increasing opportunity cost means that reallocating resources to one project will result in a progressively larger sacrifice in the output of another project.

Additional Information

  • The PPC is also called production possibility boundary:
    • This statement is correct. The PPC (Production Possibilities Curve) is also known as the production possibility boundary or frontier. It represents the maximum possible output combinations of two goods that an economy can achieve, given available resources and technology.
  • Shift of the PPC curve is nothing but economic growth:
    • Correct. When the PPC curve shifts outward, it indicates economic growth. This shift can be due to factors such as an increase in resources, technological advancements, or improvements in the efficiency of resource utilization.
    • In a financial enterprise, economic growth could mean increased investment opportunities, expansion of markets, and higher potential returns on investments.
  • Any point that lies below the PPC curve is a possible combination. But if the economy is working below the PPC curve that indicates the unused resources or unemployment:
    • This statement is accurate. Points below the PPC indicate that the economy is not utilizing all its resources efficiently, leading to underemployment or unemployment. It suggests that the economy can produce more of both goods without sacrificing the production of either.
    • For a financial enterprise, operating below the PPC might mean that the company is not utilizing its assets and resources to their fullest potential, indicating inefficiency.

questions.question: In the case of necessary goods, the law of demand cannot be operated. This was observed by the British economist:
questions.questionHtml: In the case of necessary goods, the law of demand cannot be operated. This was observed by the British economist:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sir Robert Giffen

Key Points

  • Sir Robert Giffen:
    • Sir Robert Giffen is known for his observation related to the behavior of demand for necessary goods, which led to the concept of Giffen goods.
    • Giffen goods are a type of inferior good for which an increase in the price results in an increase in quantity demanded, contrary to the law of demand.
    • These goods are typically essential items, where the income effect outweighs the substitution effect, leading to higher demand even as prices rise.

Additional Information

  • Milton Friedman:
    • Milton Friedman was an American economist known for his work on consumption analysis, monetary history, and theory, and the complexity of stabilization policy. He did not focus on the law of demand in the context of necessary goods.
  • Irving Fisher:
    • Irving Fisher was an American economist who made important contributions to the theory of interest and capital. His work did not directly address the law of demand concerning necessary goods.
  • John Maynard Keynes:
    • John Maynard Keynes was a British economist whose ideas fundamentally changed the theory and practice of macroeconomics and economic policies. He is best known for his advocacy of government intervention to achieve full employment and stable prices, not for his work on the law of demand in relation to necessary goods.

questions.question: The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India is assisted by the IA&AD to discharge his/her constitutional role. What does 'IA&AD' stand for?
questions.questionHtml: The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India is assisted by the IA&AD to discharge his/her constitutional role. What does 'IA&AD' stand for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Indian Audit and Accounts Department

Key Points

  • Indian Audit and Accounts Department (IA&AD):
    • The IA&AD is a crucial arm of the Comptroller and Auditor-General (CAG) of India, assisting in fulfilling the CAG's constitutional responsibilities.
    • It is responsible for auditing accounts of the Union and State governments and public sector organizations, ensuring transparency and accountability in financial management.
    • The department conducts performance audits, compliance audits, and financial audits to assess the efficiency and effectiveness of government operations.

Additional Information

  • Indian Audit and Accounts Distribution:
    • This option is incorrect as there is no such entity. The term "Distribution" does not align with the functions or structure of the audit and accounts framework under the CAG.
  • Internal Audit and Accounts Department:
    • This is incorrect because "Internal Audit" typically refers to internal checks within an organization, not a national-level audit body like the IA&AD, which audits external entities.
  • Indian Audit and Auditor Department:
    • This option is incorrect as it incorrectly names the department. The correct term is "Indian Audit and Accounts Department," which accurately reflects the dual roles of auditing and accounting.

questions.question: In relation to the term 'Supply', which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
questions.questionHtml: In relation to the term 'Supply', which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

options.text: Supply refers to what a firm offers for sale in market.
options.html: Supply refers to what a firm offers for sale in market.

options.text: Supply is not identified for a specified time period.
options.html: Supply is not identified for a specified time period.

options.text: Supply requires both willingness and the ability to supply.
options.html: Supply requires both willingness and the ability to supply.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Supply is not identified for a specified time period.

Key Points

  • Supply is not identified for a specified time period:
    • This statement is incorrect because supply is indeed identified for a specified time period. Supply refers to the quantity of a good or service that a firm is willing and able to offer for sale at a given price over a specified period of time. Without specifying the time period, the concept of supply would be incomplete and ambiguous.
    • In financial enterprises, understanding the time frame is crucial for planning production, inventory management, and meeting market demand efficiently.

Additional Information

  • Supply refers to what a firm offers for sale in market:
    • This statement is correct. Supply represents the quantity of a good or service that a firm is willing to sell in the market at various prices.
    • It is a fundamental concept in economics and is essential for understanding market dynamics.
  • Supply is a flow:
    • This statement is correct. Supply is considered a flow because it is measured over a period of time, such as per day, per week, or per month, rather than at a single point in time.
    • This temporal aspect distinguishes it from stock, which is measured at a particular point in time.
  • Supply requires both willingness and the ability to supply:
    • This statement is correct. For supply to be effective, a firm must be both willing and able to produce and offer the goods or services for sale.
    • In financial enterprises, this means having the necessary resources, technology, and market conditions favorable to production and sale.

questions.question: In relation to the scope of economics, which of the following statements is regarded as a traditional approach and NOT modern approach?
questions.questionHtml: In relation to the scope of economics, which of the following statements is regarded as a traditional approach and NOT modern approach?

options.text: Welfare economics and growth economics are more normative than positive.
options.html: Welfare economics and growth economics are more normative than positive.

options.text: Social problems can thus be explained by abstract theoretical tools or by empirical methods.
options.html: Social problems can thus be explained by abstract theoretical tools or by empirical methods.

options.text: The scope of economics lies in analysing economic problems and suggesting policy measures.
options.html: The scope of economics lies in analysing economic problems and suggesting policy measures.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Economics is a social science.

Key Points

  • Economics is a social science:
    • This statement reflects the traditional approach to the scope of economics. Traditionally, economics has been regarded as a social science that studies human behavior, particularly the allocation of scarce resources to meet various needs and wants.
    • It emphasizes the study of economic activities and interactions within a society, focusing on how individuals and groups make decisions about production, distribution, and consumption.

Additional Information

  • Welfare economics and growth economics are more normative than positive:
    • This statement reflects a more modern approach. Modern economics often distinguishes between positive economics (which is descriptive and based on observable phenomena) and normative economics (which involves value judgments and policy recommendations).
    • Welfare economics and growth economics, which deal with issues like income distribution and economic development, often involve normative analysis.
  • Social problems can thus be explained by abstract theoretical tools or by empirical methods:
    • This statement also reflects a modern approach, emphasizing the use of both theoretical models and empirical data to analyze and solve social and economic problems.
    • Modern economics relies heavily on quantitative methods and statistical analysis to test theories and inform policy decisions.
  • The scope of economics lies in analysing economic problems and suggesting policy measures:
    • This statement aligns with the modern approach, which focuses on applying economic theories and models to real-world problems and developing policy recommendations to address those problems.
    • Modern economists often work closely with policymakers to design and evaluate economic policies aimed at improving social welfare and economic efficiency.

questions.question: If the proportionate change in the demand is equal to the proportionate change in the price, the demand is said to be:
questions.questionHtml: If the proportionate change in the demand is equal to the proportionate change in the price, the demand is said to be:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is unitary elastic demand.

Key Points

  • Unitary elastic demand:
    • In unitary elastic demand, the percentage change in quantity demanded is exactly equal to the percentage change in price.
    • This means that total revenue remains constant when the price changes.
    • For example, if the price of a product increases by 10%, the quantity demanded will decrease by 10%.
    • This concept is crucial for businesses in financial enterprises to understand how changes in pricing can affect their revenue.

Additional Information

  • Perfectly inelastic demand:
    • In perfectly inelastic demand, the quantity demanded does not change at all when the price changes.
    • Goods with perfectly inelastic demand are typically necessities with no close substitutes.
  • Relatively elastic demand:
    • In relatively elastic demand, the percentage change in quantity demanded is greater than the percentage change in price.
    • Consumers are highly responsive to price changes for these goods.
  • Relatively inelastic demand:
    • In relatively inelastic demand, the percentage change in quantity demanded is less than the percentage change in price.
    • Consumers are less responsive to price changes for these goods.

questions.question: Which of the following definitions is INCORRECT?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following definitions is INCORRECT?

options.text: Urbanisation : Trend of migration of people from rural areas to urban areas
options.html: Urbanisation : Trend of migration of people from rural areas to urban areas

options.text: Population explosion : Rapid increase in population
options.html: Population explosion : Rapid increase in population

options.text: Density of population : Number of people living in per sq. feet of land
options.html: Density of population : Number of people living in per sq. feet of land

options.text: Demographic transition : Change in the size of population and its determinants
options.html: Demographic transition : Change in the size of population and its determinants

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Density of population: Number of people living in per sq. feet of land.

Key Points

  • Density of population: Number of people living in per sq. feet of land:
    • This definition is incorrect. The density of population is generally measured as the number of people living per square kilometer or per square mile of land, not per square foot. This measure helps in understanding how crowded or sparsely populated an area is, which is crucial for urban planning, resource allocation, and infrastructure development.
    • In the context of financial enterprises, understanding population density can help in market analysis, determining the potential customer base, and making decisions on where to open new branches or set up services.

Additional Information

  • Urbanisation: Trend of migration of people from rural areas to urban areas:
    • This definition is correct. Urbanisation involves people moving from rural to urban areas, often seeking better employment opportunities, education, and living conditions. This trend impacts financial enterprises by increasing the demand for banking services, loans, and financial products in urban areas.
  • Population explosion: Rapid increase in population:
    • This definition is correct. Population explosion refers to a sudden and rapid increase in the population. This can strain resources and infrastructure but also offers opportunities for financial enterprises to cater to a larger customer base.
  • Demographic transition: Change in the size of population and its determinants:
    • This definition is correct. Demographic transition describes the change in a population's size due to factors like birth rates, death rates, and migration. Financial enterprises analyze these changes to forecast market trends and develop long-term strategies.

questions.question: Under monopoly market, if the seller charges different prices from different customers on the basis of paying capacity of the consumer, it is said to be price discrimination of the ________.
questions.questionHtml: Under monopoly market, if the seller charges different prices from different customers on the basis of paying capacity of the consumer, it is said to be price discrimination of the ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is price discrimination of the first degree.

Key Points

  • Price discrimination of the first degree:
    • Also known as perfect price discrimination, it occurs when a monopolist charges each consumer their maximum willingness to pay.
    • This method allows the seller to capture the entire consumer surplus, converting it into additional revenue.
    • It requires detailed knowledge of each consumer's willingness to pay, which can be challenging to obtain and implement.
    • In practice, examples include personalized pricing in online markets or auctions where each bid reflects the buyer's highest valuation.

Additional Information

  • Second-degree price discrimination:
    • Incorrect in this context. This type involves charging different prices based on the quantity consumed or the version of the product. Examples include bulk discounts or different versions of software with varying features.
  • Third-degree price discrimination:
    • Incorrect here. It involves segmenting the market into distinct groups based on identifiable characteristics like age, location, or time of purchase, and charging each group a different price. Common examples are student discounts or senior citizen discounts.
  • Fourth-degree price discrimination:
    • This is not a standard term in economic theory. The recognized forms of price discrimination are primarily the first, second, and third degrees.

questions.question: Which of the following are considered as development issues in the Indian economy? (i) Low per capita income (ii) Heavy population pressure (iii) Inequality in wealth distribution
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following are considered as development issues in the Indian economy?

(i) Low per capita income

(ii) Heavy population pressure

(iii) Inequality in wealth distribution
questions.solution:
The correct answer is All (i), (ii) and (iii).

Key Points

  • Low per capita income:
    • A low per capita income indicates that on average, individuals in the economy earn relatively little. This is a fundamental development issue as it signifies a lower standard of living and economic well-being.
    • Financial enterprises thrive better in economies with higher disposable incomes where individuals and businesses can afford to invest and spend more.
  • Heavy population pressure:
    • Heavy population pressure can strain resources and infrastructure, making it difficult to sustain economic growth. It results in high demand for jobs, education, healthcare, and other services.
    • For financial enterprises, this can mean greater competition for scarce resources and customers with limited financial capacity.
  • Inequality in wealth distribution:
    • When wealth is unevenly distributed, a smaller portion of the population controls a large share of the resources, leading to social and economic disparities. This can limit economic growth and social cohesion.
    • For financial enterprises, extreme wealth inequality can lead to a saturated market at the top while the bottom remains underserved, leading to fewer opportunities for broad-based financial growth.

Additional Information

  • Only (i) and (ii):
    • This option is incorrect because it omits inequality in wealth distribution, which is a significant development issue in the Indian economy. Ignoring wealth inequality overlooks a core aspect of sustainable and inclusive economic growth.
  • Only (ii) and (iii):
    • This option is incorrect as it leaves out low per capita income, a critical measure of overall economic health and prosperity. Per capita income is vital for assessing living standards and economic progress.
  • Only (i) and (iii):
    • This option is incorrect because it excludes heavy population pressure, which significantly impacts economic development by putting a strain on resources, infrastructure, and social services.

questions.question: In relation to methods of economic study, which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
questions.questionHtml: In relation to methods of economic study, which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

options.text: Inductive method is also known as historical method 'or' statistical method.
options.html: Inductive method is also known as historical method 'or' statistical method.

options.text: Deductive method is a static analysis, inductive method is dynamic.
options.html: Deductive method is a static analysis, inductive method is dynamic.

options.text: Deductive method is also called prior method, abstract method and analytical method.
options.html: Deductive method is also called prior method, abstract method and analytical method.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Modern economists follow deductive method.

Key Points

  • Modern economists follow deductive method:
    • This statement is incorrect. Modern economists often use both inductive and deductive methods. The inductive method involves deriving general principles from specific observations, while the deductive method involves deducing specific predictions from general principles.
    • In practice, economists may start with a theory (deductive) and then test it with real-world data (inductive), or they may observe data patterns and formulate theories based on those observations.

Additional Information

  • Inductive method is also known as historical method or statistical method:
    • This statement is correct. The inductive method involves gathering data and observations to form general principles or theories, often using historical or statistical analysis.
  • Deductive method is a static analysis, inductive method is dynamic:
    • This statement is correct. The deductive method often involves static analysis where conclusions are derived from established theories. The inductive method, being based on observation and data collection, is more dynamic and adaptable to new information.
  • Deductive method is also called prior method, abstract method and analytical method:
    • This statement is correct. The deductive method is often referred to by these names because it involves reasoning from general principles or theories (prior knowledge) to specific instances.

questions.question: Which of the following agencies is responsible for formulating the fiscal policy of India?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following agencies is responsible for formulating the fiscal policy of India?

options.text: Securities and Exchange Board of India
options.html: Securities and Exchange Board of India

options.text: Ministry of Finance of the Government of India
options.html: Ministry of Finance of the Government of India

options.text: National Bank for Agricultural and Rural Development
options.html: National Bank for Agricultural and Rural Development

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ministry of Finance of the Government of India

Key Points

  • Ministry of Finance of the Government of India:
    • The Ministry of Finance is responsible for formulating and implementing the fiscal policy of India.
    • This includes managing government revenue, expenditure, and overall financial management to ensure economic stability and growth.
    • The Ministry of Finance oversees budget preparation, taxation policies, and public debt management, among other critical financial functions.

Additional Information

  • Securities and Exchange Board of India:
    • The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) regulates the securities market in India.
    • Its primary function is to protect investor interests and promote the development of the securities market.
    • SEBI does not formulate fiscal policy; its role is more focused on market regulation and oversight.
  • Reserve Bank of India:
    • The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the central bank of the country and is responsible for monetary policy, not fiscal policy.
    • RBI manages the country's money supply and interest rates to control inflation and stabilize the currency.
    • While RBI plays a crucial role in economic stability, it does not handle fiscal policy formulation.
  • National Bank for Agricultural and Rural Development:
    • The National Bank for Agricultural and Rural Development (NABARD) focuses on the development of agriculture and rural areas in India.
    • Its functions include providing credit for agriculture, small-scale industries, and other rural economic activities.
    • NABARD does not formulate fiscal policy; its role is more specialized in rural development and agricultural finance.

  • Central Statistical Organisation (CSO):

questions.question: Which of the following is a secondary function of commercial banks?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is a secondary function of commercial banks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Issuing traveller's checks.

Key Points

  • Issuing traveller's checks:
    • This is a secondary function of commercial banks. Traveller's checks are pre-printed, fixed-amount checks designed to allow the person signing them to make an unconditional payment to someone else as a result of having paid the issuer (usually a bank) for that privilege.
    • They are used primarily by people traveling to foreign countries as a safe and secure way to carry money.

Additional Information

  • Accepting demand deposits:
    • This is a primary function of commercial banks. Demand deposits are funds that are deposited in a bank account from which they can be withdrawn at any time without any advance notice.
    • They are typically used for day-to-day transactions and include checking accounts.
  • Accepting time deposits:
    • This is another primary function of commercial banks. Time deposits are interest-bearing bank deposits that have a specified date of maturity, such as certificates of deposit (CDs).
    • Funds deposited in time deposits cannot be withdrawn before the maturity date without incurring a penalty.
  • Advancing loans:
    • This is also a primary function of commercial banks. Banks provide various types of loans to individuals and businesses, including personal loans, mortgages, and business loans.
    • These loans are a significant source of income for banks through the interest charged on the borrowed amounts.

questions.question: Water supply, sanitation, health, and housing are examples of ________.
questions.questionHtml: Water supply, sanitation, health, and housing are examples of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is social infrastructure.

Key Points

  • Social Infrastructure:
    • Social infrastructure refers to the facilities and structures that support the quality of life within a community. This includes essential services like water supply, sanitation, healthcare, and housing.
    • These services are crucial for the well-being and development of individuals and communities, providing necessary living conditions and improving public health and safety.
    • In the context of a financial enterprise, investing in social infrastructure can lead to long-term societal benefits, increased productivity, and economic stability.

Additional Information

  • Economic Infrastructure:
    • Economic infrastructure includes physical systems like transportation networks, energy supply, and communication systems. These are essential for economic activities and production processes.
    • While vital for economic growth, these do not directly address individual quality of life aspects such as health or housing.
  • Collateral Infrastructure:
    • This term is not commonly used in the context of infrastructure. Collateral typically refers to assets pledged as security for a loan, not a category of infrastructure.
  • Collusive Infrastructure:
    • This is not a standard term in infrastructure discussions. Collusion refers to secret cooperation for deceitful purposes, which is unrelated to types of infrastructure.

questions.question: While usage of the information technology (IT) in banking contributes to efficiency, it brings along with it certain issues, such as: (i) Issues of technology selection with strategic, financial and compliance considerations (ii) Issues related to process management to ensure cost-effective and timely service delivery (iii) Issues related to security of customer and business data at access
questions.questionHtml:
While usage of the information technology (IT) in banking contributes to efficiency, it brings along with it certain issues, such as:

(i) Issues of technology selection with strategic, financial and compliance considerations

(ii) Issues related to process management to ensure cost-effective and timely service delivery

(iii) Issues related to security of customer and business data at access
questions.solution:
The correct answer is All of (i), (ii) and (iii).

Key Points

  • All of (i), (ii), and (iii):
    • Issues of technology selection with strategic, financial, and compliance considerations:
      • Financial enterprises must carefully select technology that aligns with their strategic goals, budget constraints, and regulatory requirements. Poor selection can result in inefficiencies and non-compliance with regulations.
    • Issues related to process management to ensure cost-effective and timely service delivery:
      • Efficient process management is crucial for banks to deliver services cost-effectively and within timelines. Mismanagement can lead to increased costs and customer dissatisfaction.
    • Issues related to security of customer and business data at access:
      • Data security is paramount in banking. Banks must protect sensitive customer and business data from unauthorized access and breaches, which can lead to financial losses and reputational damage.

Additional Information

  • Only (i) and (iii):
    • This option is incorrect as it overlooks the critical aspect of process management (ii), which is essential for cost-effective and timely service delivery in the banking sector.
  • Only (ii) and (iii):
    • This option is incorrect because it ignores the importance of technology selection (i), which is vital for ensuring strategic, financial, and compliance alignment.
  • Only (i) and (ii):
    • This option is incorrect as it fails to consider the significant issue of data security (iii), which is crucial for protecting customer and business information.

questions.question: ________ explains how much change in the price of one commodity leads to how much change in the demand for another commodity.
questions.questionHtml: ________ explains how much change in the price of one commodity leads to how much change in the demand for another commodity.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Cross elasticity of demand.

Key Points

  • Cross elasticity of demand:
    • This concept measures the responsiveness of the quantity demanded for one good when the price of another good changes.
    • It is particularly useful in understanding the relationship between complementary goods (e.g., printers and ink cartridges) and substitute goods (e.g., tea and coffee).
    • A positive cross elasticity indicates substitute goods, while a negative cross elasticity indicates complementary goods.
    • For financial enterprises, understanding cross elasticity helps in strategic pricing and marketing decisions, especially in competitive markets.

Additional Information

  • Income elasticity of demand:
    • This measures how the quantity demanded of a good changes as consumer income changes.
    • It is not related to the price of another commodity but rather to changes in income levels.
  • Price elasticity of demand:
    • This measures the responsiveness of the quantity demanded of a good to a change in its own price.
    • It does not involve the price or demand of another commodity.
  • Expense elasticity of demand:
    • This term is not commonly used in economic literature and may be confused with income elasticity or price elasticity.
    • It generally does not refer to the relationship between two different commodities.

questions.question: _______ is most common in industries like agriculture, tourism, hotel, catering, etc.
questions.questionHtml: _______ is most common in industries like agriculture, tourism, hotel, catering, etc.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Seasonal unemployment.

Key Points

  • Seasonal Unemployment:
    • Seasonal unemployment occurs when people are unemployed at particular times of the year when demand for labor is lower than usual.
    • This type of unemployment is common in industries like agriculture, tourism, hotel, and catering, where the demand for labor fluctuates with the seasons.
    • For example, agricultural workers may be in high demand during planting and harvest seasons but may face unemployment during the off-season.
    • Similarly, tourism-related jobs may surge during holiday seasons and decline during off-peak periods.

Additional Information

  • Structural Unemployment:
    • Structural unemployment occurs due to a mismatch between the skills of the workforce and the demands of the job market.This is often due to technological advancements or shifts in the economy, rendering certain skills obsolete.
    • This type of unemployment is not typically seasonal and is more related to long-term changes in the economy.
  • Cyclical Unemployment:
    • Cyclical unemployment is related to the economic cycle of boom and bust.
    • During periods of economic downturn or recession, businesses reduce their workforce, leading to higher unemployment.
    • This type of unemployment is not tied to specific seasons but rather the overall economic climate.
  • Frictional Unemployment:
    • Frictional unemployment occurs when people are temporarily unemployed while transitioning from one job to another.
    • This type of unemployment is usually short-term and is a natural part of the job search process.
    • It is not typically associated with seasonal industries.

questions.question: What powers does the Comptroller and Auditor General of India have to perform his role? (i) Power to inspect any office or organisation subject to his audit. (ii) Power to examine all transactions and question the executive. (iii) Power to call for any records, papers, documents from any audited entity. (iv) Power to decide the extent and manner of audit.
questions.questionHtml:
What powers does the Comptroller and Auditor General of India have to perform his role?

(i) Power to inspect any office or organisation subject to his audit.

(ii) Power to examine all transactions and question the executive.

(iii) Power to call for any records, papers, documents from any audited entity.

(iv) Power to decide the extent and manner of audit.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is All (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv)

Key Points

  • Power to inspect any office or organisation subject to his audit:
    • The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) has the authority to inspect any office or organization that falls under his audit jurisdiction. This ensures that the CAG can thoroughly examine the financial records and practices of the entities being audited.
  • Power to examine all transactions and question the executive:
    • The CAG has the power to scrutinize all financial transactions conducted by the audited entities. This includes questioning the executive decisions related to financial matters to ensure accountability and transparency.
  • Power to call for any records, papers, documents from any audited entity:
    • The CAG can request any relevant records, papers, or documents from the entities being audited. This access is crucial for conducting a comprehensive audit and verifying the accuracy of financial statements.
  • Power to decide the extent and manner of audit:
    • The CAG has the discretion to determine the scope and methodology of the audit. This flexibility allows the CAG to tailor the audit process to effectively address the specific financial practices and risks of each entity.

Additional Information

  • Only (i), (ii) and (iv):
    • Incorrect because it excludes the CAG's power to call for any records, papers, documents from any audited entity, which is essential for a thorough audit.
  • Only (ii) and (iii):
    • Incorrect because it omits the CAG's power to inspect any office or organization and to decide the extent and manner of audit, both of which are critical for effective auditing.
  • Only (i) and (ii):
    • Incorrect as it leaves out the CAG's power to call for any records and to decide the extent and manner of audit, which are necessary for a complete and effective audit process.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of 'Land and labour' as a factor of production?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is NOT a feature of 'Land and labour' as a factor of production?

options.text: Land cannot be moved from one place to another, unlike other factors.
options.html: Land cannot be moved from one place to another, unlike other factors.

options.text: If a worker does not find work on a particular day, the labour is lost for that day.
options.html: If a worker does not find work on a particular day, the labour is lost for that day.

options.text: Land is a gift of nature.
options.html: Land is a gift of nature.

options.text: There is no difference in the efficiency of labour.
options.html: There is no difference in the efficiency of labour.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is There is no difference in the efficiency of labour.

Key Points

  • There is no difference in the efficiency of labour:
    • This statement is incorrect because the efficiency of labour varies based on several factors such as skill level, experience, motivation, health, and working conditions.
    • In a financial enterprise, employees with higher skills and better training are generally more efficient and productive, contributing more effectively to the company's goals.
    • Labour efficiency impacts the overall productivity and profitability of an organization, making it a critical factor in production.

Additional Information

  • Land cannot be moved from one place to another, unlike other factors:
    • This statement is correct. Land is a fixed resource and cannot be relocated, making it unique compared to other factors of production like labour, capital, and entrepreneurship.
  • If a worker does not find work on a particular day, the labour is lost for that day:
    • This statement is correct. Labour is perishable and cannot be stored for future use. If not utilized, the potential productivity for that day is permanently lost.
  • Land is a gift of nature:
    • This statement is correct. Land is naturally available and not created by human effort, making it a fundamental resource for production activities.

questions.question: In relation to fiscal deficit, which of the following is correct?
questions.questionHtml: In relation to fiscal deficit, which of the following is correct?

options.text: Fiscal deficit = Primary deficit - Interest payments
options.html: Fiscal deficit = Primary deficit - Interest payments

options.text: Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure - Total receipts excluding borrowings
options.html: Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure - Total receipts excluding borrowings

options.text: Greater fiscal deficit implies lesser borrowing by the government
options.html: Greater fiscal deficit implies lesser borrowing by the government

options.text: Fiscal deficit = Total revenue expenditure – Total revenue receipts
options.html: Fiscal deficit = Total revenue expenditure – Total revenue receipts

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure - Total receipts excluding borrowings

Key Points

  • Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure - Total receipts excluding borrowings:
    • This formula accurately defines the fiscal deficit. It represents the gap between the government's total expenditure and its total revenue (excluding any borrowings).
    • The fiscal deficit indicates how much the government needs to borrow to meet its expenditure requirements.
    • A higher fiscal deficit implies greater borrowing needs, influencing the overall economic stability and interest rates.

Additional Information

  • Fiscal deficit = Primary deficit - Interest payments:
    • This statement is incorrect. The primary deficit is calculated as the fiscal deficit minus interest payments. Therefore, the fiscal deficit includes the primary deficit and interest payments, not the other way around.
  • Greater fiscal deficit implies lesser borrowing by the government:
    • This statement is incorrect. A greater fiscal deficit actually implies greater borrowing needs by the government to cover the shortfall between its expenditure and revenue.
  • Fiscal deficit = Total revenue expenditure – Total revenue receipts:
    • This statement is incorrect. While it partially captures the concept, it misses out on capital expenditure and receipts which are also part of the total expenditure and total receipts, respectively.

questions.question: In relation to Production Possibilities Curve (PPC), which of the following statements is INCORRECT ?
questions.questionHtml: In relation to Production Possibilities Curve (PPC), which of the following statements is INCORRECT ?

options.text: The slope of the Production Possibility Curve at any given point is called marginal rate of transformation.
options.html: The slope of the Production Possibility Curve at any given point is called marginal rate of transformation.

options.text: The Production Possibilities Curve is also called production possibility frontier.
options.html: The Production Possibilities Curve is also called production possibility frontier.

options.text: The Production Possibilities Curve always slopes upwards from left to right.
options.html: The Production Possibilities Curve always slopes upwards from left to right.

options.text: Production Possibilities Curve is concave to the origin because marginal rate of transformation goes on increasing.
options.html: Production Possibilities Curve is concave to the origin because marginal rate of transformation goes on increasing.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is The Production Possibilities Curve always slopes upwards from left to right.

Key Points

  • The Production Possibilities Curve always slopes upwards from left to right:
    • This statement is incorrect. The Production Possibilities Curve (PPC) typically slopes downwards from left to right, reflecting the trade-off between the production of two goods. As more of one good is produced, less of the other can be produced due to limited resources.

Additional Information

  • The slope of the Production Possibility Curve at any given point is called marginal rate of transformation:
    • This statement is correct. The marginal rate of transformation (MRT) represents the rate at which one good must be sacrificed to produce an additional unit of another good, indicating the opportunity cost.
  • The Production Possibilities Curve is also called production possibility frontier:
    • This is correct. The Production Possibility Frontier (PPF) is another term for the PPC, illustrating the maximum feasible amount of two commodities that a business can produce with available resources and technology.
  • Production Possibilities Curve is concave to the origin because marginal rate of transformation goes on increasing:
    • This is accurate. The PPC is typically concave to the origin because resources are not perfectly adaptable for the production of both goods, leading to increasing opportunity costs as production shifts from one good to the other.

questions.question: The term 'Demand' refers to the ________ of goods or services that buyers are willing and able to purchase at various prices during a given period of time.
questions.questionHtml: The term 'Demand' refers to the ________ of goods or services that buyers are willing and able to purchase at various prices during a given period of time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is quantity.

Key Points

  • Quantity:
    • In the context of financial enterprise, 'demand' specifically refers to the amount or quantity of goods or services that consumers are prepared to buy at various price levels over a certain time period.
    • Understanding demand is crucial for businesses to make informed decisions about production, pricing, and marketing strategies.
    • Accurate demand forecasting helps in managing inventory levels, reducing costs, and maximizing profits.

Additional Information

  • Usability:
    • This refers to how user-friendly or practical a product or service is, but it does not capture the economic concept of demand.
    • While usability can influence demand, it is not the definition of demand itself.
  • Quality:
    • Quality denotes the standard of a product or service, which can affect its desirability and price, but it is not synonymous with demand.
    • High-quality products might have higher demand, but 'quality' alone does not define demand.
  • Ability:
    • Ability could refer to the capability of consumers to purchase goods or services, which is a component of demand but not the full definition.
    • Demand encompasses both the willingness and ability to purchase, not just the ability.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of economic infrastructure?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is NOT an example of economic infrastructure?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Water supply.

Key Points

  • Water supply is NOT an example of economic infrastructure:
    • Economic infrastructure refers to the fundamental facilities and systems that support economic activities and growth. These typically include transportation, power, and irrigation systems.
    • While water supply is crucial for human survival and residential needs, it is generally classified under social infrastructure rather than economic infrastructure.
    • Social infrastructure includes facilities and services that support the quality of life, such as healthcare, education, and water supply systems.

Additional Information

  • Transportation:
    • Transportation infrastructure includes roads, railways, airports, and ports which are essential for the movement of goods and services, thereby playing a critical role in economic activities.
  • Power:
    • Power infrastructure involves the generation, transmission, and distribution of electricity. Reliable power supply is vital for industrial operations, commercial activities, and overall economic development.
  • Irrigation:
    • Irrigation infrastructure includes canals, dams, and pipelines that facilitate the supply of water to agricultural lands. Efficient irrigation systems are crucial for enhancing agricultural productivity and supporting the agricultural economy.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of elasticity of demand ?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is NOT a type of elasticity of demand ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Product quality elasticity of demand.

Key Points

  • Product quality elasticity of demand:
    • This term is not a recognized type of elasticity of demand in economic theory.
    • Elasticity of demand typically refers to how the quantity demanded of a good responds to changes in price, income, or the price of related goods, not to changes in product quality.
    • While product quality can influence demand, it is not measured using elasticity of demand.

Additional Information

  • Cross elasticity of demand:
    • This measures the responsiveness of the quantity demanded for one good to a change in the price of another good. It is particularly useful for understanding the relationship between substitute or complementary goods.
  • Price elasticity of demand:
    • This measures the responsiveness of the quantity demanded to a change in the price of the good itself. It helps businesses understand how changes in price can affect their sales volume and revenue.
  • Income elasticity of demand:
    • This measures the responsiveness of the quantity demanded to a change in consumer income. It helps to categorize goods as normal or inferior and understand how demand shifts with economic cycles.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a central problem of economy?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is NOT a central problem of economy?
questions.solution:
The answer is When to produce

Key Points

  • When to produce:
    • This is not considered a central problem of the economy. Central problems typically revolve around the allocation of resources and distribution of goods and services, rather than the timing of production.
    • In a financial enterprise, timing can be relevant for inventory management or market strategy, but it does not address the core economic questions.

Additional Information

  • For whom to produce:
    • This is a central economic problem that addresses the distribution of goods and services among different segments of society.
    • It involves decisions about targeting different consumer groups, which is crucial for financial enterprises aiming to maximize market reach and profitability.
  • What to produce:
    • This is another core economic issue that involves deciding which goods and services should be produced based on consumer needs and resource availability.
    • Financial enterprises must determine the most profitable products or services to offer to meet market demand.
  • How to produce:
    • This problem focuses on the methods and processes of production, including the technology and resources used.
    • For financial enterprises, this could mean choosing the most efficient operational processes to minimize costs and maximize output.

questions.question: _______ shows the proportionate change in demand with respect to proportionate change in income.
questions.questionHtml: _______ shows the proportionate change in demand with respect to proportionate change in income.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Income elasticity of demand.

Key Points

  • Income elasticity of demand:
    • It measures how the quantity demanded of a good responds to a change in consumer income.
    • A higher income elasticity indicates that demand for the good is more sensitive to changes in income.
    • For financial enterprises, understanding income elasticity helps in predicting how changes in economic conditions will affect product demand.
    • Goods with high income elasticity are often luxury items, whereas goods with low or negative income elasticity are necessities or inferior goods.

Additional Information

  • Product quality elasticity of demand:
    • This concept is not commonly used in economics. It might refer to how demand changes with changes in product quality, but it is not a standard measure.
  • Cross elasticity of demand:
    • Measures the responsiveness of demand for one good to a change in the price of another good.
    • This is relevant for understanding substitute or complementary goods, not changes in income.
  • Price elasticity of demand:
    • Measures how the quantity demanded of a good responds to a change in its price.
    • This is crucial for pricing strategies but does not involve changes in consumer income.

questions.question: In the _______ the producer can determine the price of the commodity and hence, the producer is said to be the price maker in the market. Maximisation of profits is the sole objective.
questions.questionHtml: In the _______ the producer can determine the price of the commodity and hence, the producer is said to be the price maker in the market. Maximisation of profits is the sole objective.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the monopoly market.

Key Points

  • Monopoly Market:
    • In a monopoly market, a single producer or a single firm controls the entire supply of a product or service, and thus, has significant control over the market price.
    • As the sole provider, the monopolist can set prices without worrying about competition, making them a price maker.
    • The primary objective in a monopoly is profit maximization. The monopolist will determine the price and output level that yields the highest possible profit.
    • Examples include utility companies and certain patented pharmaceutical products.

Additional Information

  • Oligopoly Market:
    • In an oligopoly, a few large firms dominate the market. While these firms have some control over prices, they are interdependent and must consider the potential reactions of competitors when making pricing decisions.
    • Examples include the automobile industry and the airline industry.
  • Duopoly Market:
    • A duopoly is a specific type of oligopoly where only two firms dominate the market. These firms have significant control over prices but still must consider the actions of their sole competitor.
    • Examples include the commercial aircraft manufacturing market dominated by Boeing and Airbus.
  • Perfect Competition Market:
    • In a perfect competition market, there are many sellers and buyers, and no single seller can influence the market price. All firms are price takers, meaning they must accept the market price as given.
    • Examples include agricultural markets, where no single farmer can influence the price of crops.
